7505.description_text: We’ve all felt the effects of a bad night’s sleep – tiredness, irritability, and trouble focusing just to name a few. Sleep and relaxation are essential for keeping our body and mind well rested and recovering between days. Having a regular evening routine that supports your wellness can help you wind down, so you sleep better. Myvitamins’ Relax Bundle includes two popular wellness supplements both in a convenient capsule form – ashwagandha and inositol. Ashwagandha KSM-66 (30 capsules) Ashwagandha, also called Indian Ginseng, is a herb that’s been used as an adaptogen in traditional ayurvedic medicine for hundreds of years. Each capsule contains 500mg of full-spectrum ashwagandha KSM-66 – a natural, convenient addition to your daily wellness routine. Inositol (30 capsules) Inositol is sometimes called vitamin B8, but it’s actually a natural sugar found in fruits like oranges and melons. It’s also become an increasingly popular supplement in recent years because of its vitamin-like properties. With 750mg inositol in each capsule, it’s a quick and easy way to top up your daily inositol intake. So to help regulate your hormones and get you feeling your best, we’ve formulated these Hormone Gummies with vitamin B6 (1). Our Hormone Gummies also include a unique combination of evening primrose oil, organic flaxseed oils, ashwagandha and rhodiola extracts. Ashwagandha and rhodiola plants are both adaptogens, which have been used for thousands of years in Ayurvedic medicine. Evening primrose oil is another botanical with a long history of traditional medicinal use. Expertly formulated with vitamins, minerals, and botanicals that contribute to normal energy-yielding metabolism, immune function, and psychological ... Support your daily wellbeing with the ultimate female wellness bundle - combining our Women’s Multivitamin, Women’s Bio-Balance, and Cranberry & D-Mannose Gummies. Expertly formulated with vitamins, minerals, and botanicals that contribute to normal energy-yielding metabolism, immune function, and psychological balance, while supporting overall female wellbeing. All the nutrients you need in one delicious gummy. 16 Key Ingredients Collagen Collagen is the most abundant protein in the body, acting as a structural building block for tissues like skin, bones, tendons, ligaments, and cartilage. Sodium Hyaluronate Sodium hyaluronate is a naturally occurring substance in the body, primarily found in the skin, connective tissues, and eyes. Lactobacillus Acidophilus A strain of beneficial bacteria found in the digestive system. These friendly bacteria target the gut where 70% of the immune system is located. Co-Enzyme Q10 A vitamin-like compound naturally present in the cells of the human body, specifically found in the organs that have high energy demands such as the heart, liver, kidneys and the skeletal muscle. Choline Choline is involved in cell membrane structure and the transport of fats in the body. It contributes to liver function and it is a precursor for acetylcholine, which is a neurotransmitter. Chromium Helps maintain stable blood sugar levels, supporting metabolism alongside fibre intake. Selenium Selenium is an antioxidant that contributes to the protection of cells from oxidative stress, supporting overall skin health. It also plays an important role in supporting the immune system. Selenium also contributes to the maintenance of hair and nails. Iodine Iodine is an essential trace element that is required for the synthesis of thyroid hormones, which regulate the metabolism, growth and development. Iodine contributes to cognitive function, nervous system activity, and maintaining healthy skin. Zinc Zinc contributes to DNA synthesis, cognitive function, fertility and reproduction, protein synthesis, and the maintenance of bones. It also supports the metabolism of carbohydrates, fatty acids, macronutrients, and Vitamin A, as well as acid-base metabolism. Zinc also contributes to the maintenance of hair, skin, nails, vision, immune system function, and testosterone levels in the blood. It helps protect cells from oxidative stress and plays a role in the process of cell division. Calcium Calcium supports the growth and maintenance of healthy bones and teeth. Inadequate intake of calcium can increase the risk of developing osteoporosis. Calcium also plays a role in nerve function, blood clotting, and maintaining healthy muscles. Calcium's significance encompasses multiple phases throughout one's life. Pantothenic Acid Pantothenic acid, also known as vitamin B5, plays a role in the body. It contributes to the synthesis and metabolism of steroid hormones, vitamin D, and some neurotransmitters. Pantothenic acid also supports energy metabolism and helps reduce tiredness. Biotin Plays a role in supporting healthy hair and skin, as it is involved in the production of keratin, a protein essential for their structure and strength. Biotin also aids in the metabolism of carbohydrates, fats, and proteins, contributing to energy production and nutrient utilisation. Vitamin B12 Vitamin B12 supports energy metabolism and psychological function; which is important for mood. It also contributes to red blood cell formation and reduces tiredness. Sodium Hyaluronate Sodium hyaluronate is a naturally occurring substance in the body, primarily found in the skin, connective tissues, and eyes. Co-Enzyme Q10 A vitamin-like compound naturally present in the cells of the human body, specifically found in the organs that have high energy demands such as the heart, liver, kidneys and the skeletal muscle. Choline Choline is involved in cell membrane structure and the transport of fats in the body. It contributes to liver function and it is a precursor for acetylcholine, which is a neurotransmitter. Chromium Helps maintain stable blood sugar levels, supporting metabolism alongside fibre intake. Selenium Selenium is an antioxidant that contributes to the protection of cells from oxidative stress, supporting overall skin health. It also plays an important role in supporting the immune system. Selenium also contributes to the maintenance of hair and nails. Iodine Iodine is an essential trace element that is required for the synthesis of thyroid hormones, which regulate the metabolism. Iodine contributes to cognitive function, nervous system activity, and maintaining skin. Zinc Zinc contributes to cognitive function, fertility and reproduction, protein synthesis, and the maintenance of bones. It also contributes to the maintenance of hair, skin, nails, vision, immune system function, and testosterone levels in the blood. It helps protect cells from oxidative stress and plays a role in the process of cell division. Calcium Calcium supports the growth and maintenance of healthy bones and teeth. Inadequate intake of calcium can increase the risk of developing osteoporosis. Calcium also plays a role in nerve function, blood clotting, and maintaining healthy muscles. Calcium's significance encompasses multiple phases throughout one's life. Pantothenic Acid Pantothenic acid contributes to the synthesis and metabolism of steroid hormones, vitamin D, and some neurotransmitters. It also supports energy metabolism and helps reduce tiredness. Biotin Plays a role in supporting hair and skin. Biotin also aids in the metabolism of carbohydrates, fats, and proteins, contributing to energy production and nutrient utilisation. Vitamin B12 Vitamin B12 supports energy metabolism and psychological function. It also contributes to red blood cell formation and reduces tiredness. Vitamin B6 Vitamin B6 contributes to energy metabolism, the functioning of the nervous & immune systems, psychological function, hormonal regulation, and the reduction of tiredness. Vitamin C Vitamin C contributes to immune system function, collagen formation, energy metabolism, and the functioning of the nervous system. It also helps to protect cells from oxidative stress, reduces fatigue, and regenerates vitamin E. Vitamin D It supports calcium absorption, contributing to the maintenance of bones. All the nutrients you need in one delicious gummy. 15 Key Ingredients Folic Acid Folic acid, also known as Vitamin B9, is a water-soluble B-vitamin that plays an important role in cell division, DNA synthesis, and red blood cell formation. It is particularly important during periods of rapid growth, such as pregnancy and early development. It contributes to the development of the neural tube in the early stages of pregnancy. The neural tube eventually develops into the baby's brain and spinal cord. It's recommended by the NHS to start taking a daily supplement of 400 micrograms of folic acid ideally before conception and continue until the 12th week of pregnancy. Vitamin D Vitamin D contributes to the normal functioning of the immune system, the maintenance of normal bones, teeth, and muscle function, and supports the absorption and utilisation of calcium and phosphorus in the body. It also helps to maintain normal blood calcium levels and plays a role in the process of cell division. Vitamin E Vitamin E is well-known as an antioxidant that contributes to the protection of cells from oxidative stress. Vitamin B6 Vitamin B6 contributes to energy metabolism, functioning of the nervous & immune systems, psychological function, red blood cell formation, hormonal regulation, and reduces fatigue. Vitamin B12 Vitamin B12 contributes to energy metabolism, functioning of the immune & nervous systems, red blood cell formation, and reduces tiredness. Vitamin B12 also plays a role in the process of cell division. Pantothenic Acid Pantothenic acid is necessary for the creation of important reproductive hormones. Choline Choline is involved in cell membrane structure and the transport of fats in the body. It contributes to liver function and it is a precursor for acetylcholine, which is a neurotransmitter. Iron Iron is an essential mineral involved in the formation of red blood cells and haemoglobin, which are necessary for transporting oxygen throughout the body. Your body uses iron to make haemoglobin, a protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen from the lungs to all parts of the body, and myoglobin, a protein that provides oxygen to muscles. Iron is important for foetal development, particularly for oxygen transport, red blood cell production, and brain development. Iodine Iodine is an essential trace element that is required for the synthesis of thyroid hormones, which regulate the metabolism, growth and development. Iodine contributes to cognitive function, nervous system activity, and maintaining healthy skin. It is crucial during pregnancy for the healthy development of the baby's brain and nervous system. Adequate iodine intake is particularly important in the first trimester when the baby's thyroid is not yet functional. Copper Copper contributes to immune function, nervous system activity, and energy-yielding metabolism. It also supports the maintenance of connective tissues, hair and skin pigmentation, iron transport, and helps to protect cells from oxidative stress. Co-Enzyme Q10 A vitamin-like compound naturally present in the cells of the human body, specifically found in the organs that have high energy demands such as the heart, liver, kidneys and the skeletal muscle. It has been researched and is seen to be linked to follicular health. Co-Enzyme Q10 plays a role in the mitochondrial electron support chain, where energy is produced at a cellular level. Lactobacilli These beneficial bacteria help maintain a healthy vaginal microbiome, creating an acidic environment that supports the growth of good bacteria. Biotin Biotin contributes to energy metabolism, functioning of the nervous system, psychological function, macronutrient metabolism, and the maintenance of skin, hair, and mucous membranes. Zinc Zinc contributes to DNA synthesis, cognitive function, fertility and reproduction, protein synthesis, and the maintenance of bones. It also supports the metabolism of carbohydrates, fatty acids, macronutrients, and Vitamin A, as well as acid-base metabolism. Zinc also contributes to the maintenance of hair, skin, nails, vision, immune system function, and testosterone levels in the blood. It helps protect cells from oxidative stress and plays a role in the process of cell division. Selenium Selenium contributes to the function of the immune system and thyroid, supports hair and nail maintenance, and helps to protect cells from oxidative stress. Packed with 17 essential vitamins and minerals, this delicious supplement is formulated to fill nutritional gaps and support energy metabolism, immune function, and overall well-being. One gummy with countless benefits. Support your everyday vitality with Novomins Multivitamin Gummies-your go-to daily dose of wellness. Packed with 17 essential vitamins and minerals, this delicious supplement is formulated to fill nutritional gaps and support energy metabolism, immune function, and overall well-being. One gummy with countless benefits. All the nutrients you need in one delicious gummy. 16 Key Ingredients Vitamin A Vitamin A supports healthy vision, the immune system, reproduction, growth, and development. Vitamin A also contributes to the immune system. Vitamin C Vitamin C contributes to immune system function, collagen formation, energy metabolism, and the functioning of the nervous system & psychological processes. It also helps to protect cells from oxidative stress, reduces tiredness, regenerates vitamin E, and enhances the absorption of iron. Vitamin E Vitamin E is an antioxidant that contributes to the protection of cells from oxidative stress. This helps maintain the function of cells throughout the body. Vitamin B6 Vitamin B6 contributes to energy metabolism, functioning of the nervous & immune systems, psychological function, hormonal regulation, and reduces fatigue. Folic Acid Folic acid, also known as folate, plays a role in several bodily functions. It contributes to blood formation and supports the immune system. Folate also contributes to psychological function and helps reduce tiredness. Vitamin B12 Vitamin B12 reduces tiredness and contributes to energy metabolism. Vitamin B12 also contributes to red blood cell formation and the immune system. Individuals following vegetarian or vegan diets may have a higher risk of Vitamin B12 deficiency, as this vitamin is primarily found in animal-derived foods. Supplementation can help maintain adequate Vitamin B12 levels to support overall health and well-being. Biotin Plays a role in supporting healthy hair and skin, as it is involved in the production of keratin, a protein essential for their structure and strength. Biotin also aids in the metabolism of carbohydrates, fats, and proteins, contributing to energy production and nutrient utilisation. Pantothenic Acid Pantothenic acid, also known as vitamin B5, plays a role in the body. It contributes to the synthesis and metabolism of steroid hormones, vitamin D, and some neurotransmitters. Pantothenic acid also supports energy metabolism and helps reduce tiredness. Zinc Zinc contributes to DNA synthesis, cognitive function, fertility and reproduction, protein synthesis, and the maintenance of bones. It also supports the metabolism of carbohydrates, fatty acids, macronutrients, and Vitamin A, as well as acid-base metabolism. Zinc also contributes to the maintenance of hair, skin, nails, vision, immune system function, and testosterone levels in the blood. It helps protect cells from oxidative stress and plays a role in the process of cell division. Copper Copper is an essential mineral that contributes to the maintenance of hair and skin pigmentation by supporting melanin production. It also plays a role in the formation of connective tissue, which helps maintain skin structure. Selenium Selenium is an antioxidant that contributes to the protection of cells from oxidative stress, supporting overall skin health. It also plays an important role in the function of the immune system. Cranberry Extract Cranberry extract is derived from cranberries, which contain naturally occurring compounds like proanthocyanidins (PACs). Cranberries are commonly consumed and valued for their natural properties. Amla Extract Amla extract, derived from the Indian gooseberry (Emblica officinalis), is a natural source of vitamin C and polyphenols. Vitamin C is a powerful antioxidant that contributes to the protection of cells from oxidative stress and supports the immune system. Vitamin B2 Vitamin B2, also known as riboflavin, is important for general health and well-being. It contributes to energy metabolism by helping convert food into usable energy for the body. Riboflavin also contributes to the maintenance of skin and vision, and it supports the functioning of the nervous system. Chia Oil Chia oil is a nutrient-rich oil extracted from chia seeds and is a source of alpha-linolenic acid (ALA), an omega-3 fatty acid. Alpha-linolenic acid contributes to the maintenance of blood cholesterol levels. Chia oil also contains naturally occurring nutrients that support overall health. Lycopene Lycopene is a natural pigment found in red fruits and vegetables like tomatoes and watermelons, giving them their vibrant colour. It is included in some products for its nutritional properties.
